headline: Democrats' gains, a Brampton plant fight, a U.S. flight shutdown and trade talks on two fronts
summary: Democrats added a Mississippi Senate seat and two governorships to their midterm sweep, then opened a leadership contest of their own. Hopes for an Iran deal rose and faded while oil still fell for a second week, U.S. wholesale inflation hit 6.5%, and Nvidia's chief executive resigned. In Ontario, Stellantis's sale of the Brampton plant set off a confrontation with Ottawa; a nationwide U.S. ground stop cancelled cross-border flights from Toronto, and Carney wrapped up trade talks with the Philippines while saying a U.S. deal must protect the auto sector.

top.headline: Democrats' sweep grows; Van Hollen challenges Schumer for Senate leader
top.what: Democrats added a Mississippi Senate seat and the Kansas and Alaska governorships to their midterm wins, and Mary Peltola is close to 50% in Alaska's uncalled Senate race. Sen. Chris Van Hollen then challenged Chuck Schumer for majority leader, with a vote set for Dec. 1.
top.why: The size and leadership of the new Democratic majority will decide how hard Congress pushes back on tariffs that hit Canada.

top.headline: Iran deal hopes fade; tankers reported hit by mines as oil still falls on the week
top.what: Oil dipped below US$90 on hopes of a deal, rebounded when Trump said none was needed, and ended the week near US$96. Iran reported up to four tankers hit by mines, and Trump is said to be holding off on new strikes for now.
top.why: Oil prices are driving inflation and interest rates in Canada, and gas prices in the GTA follow crude within days.

top.headline: Ottawa threatens to sue Stellantis over Brampton sale, then offers a package to stop it
top.what: Stellantis agreed to sell its idle Brampton plant to armoured-vehicle maker Roshel; Ottawa served a notice of default over $529 million in subsidy commitments, then joined Ontario in pitching a rescue package. Carney said Saturday that Ottawa is not satisfied with the company.
top.why: Thousands of Peel Region auto and parts jobs, and hundreds of millions in public money, depend on the outcome.

top.headline: FAA stops all U.S. departures for more than four hours after network failure
top.what: An overloaded router during contractor work halted U.S. departures on Friday; about 12,000 flights could not be completed and thousands more were cancelled Saturday. Pearson lost more than 120 cross-border flights.
top.why: Cross-border travel from Toronto was disrupted through the weekend, and the failure has renewed pressure to modernize U.S. air traffic control.

top.headline: Carney says U.S. trade deal is closer but must keep auto sector viable
top.what: After a call with Trump and his trade team, Carney said talks are progressing but that Canada will not sign a deal that undermines its auto industry. Earlier in the week Ottawa widened tariff relief and its ambassador warned tariffs are chilling investment.
top.why: The terms on autos will shape manufacturing jobs across Ontario.

top.headline: U.S. wholesale inflation reaches 6.5%, highest since 2022
top.what: Producer prices rose 6.5% from a year earlier in October; U.S. stocks slipped Friday but still gained more than 2% on the week.
top.why: The data keeps the Federal Reserve, and by extension the Bank of Canada, leaning toward higher interest rates in December.

top.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns; scandal puts Commerce Secretary Lutnick under pressure
top.what: Huang stepped down as chief executive amid a scandal over chip sales to a firm suspected of supplying China, and Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly blamed Lutnick's department for delays in restricting the sales.
top.why: Nvidia is one of the largest holdings in index funds and pensions, and the affair has reached Trump's cabinet.

top.headline: Canada and the Philippines conclude free-trade negotiations
top.what: Carney and President Marcos announced in Manila that talks are complete, with signing targeted for 2027; Ottawa says a wider deal with Southeast Asian nations is substantially concluded.
top.why: It is the first concrete result of Ottawa's push to rely less on the U.S. market.
